context.note: ICU plural (RFC §2.9 digits policy: Latin numerals): the count is the raw integer of live subagents. Zero never reaches this key — format_agents returns the empty string so the segment disappears rather than reporting '0 agents'. No fixed cell cap: the band's drop ladder (drop_ladder) sheds whole segments by width.

Rendered only while the runtime is being bound (OperatorApp._push_starting_band); the caption carries the whole meaning and is ALWAYS spelled out. Outranks the working word (UX round 1, U4): a prompt accepted before the viewer attaches must keep saying the attach is pending.

Suppressed while the shimmer already shows activity (shimmer_enabled): the accent glyph is the signal and this word is only its caption. One word by design; it rides at the end of the band's left side.

ICU plural (RFC §2.9 digits policy: Latin numerals): the count is the raw integer of backgrounded shell jobs. Zero never reaches this key — format_jobs returns the empty string so the segment disappears. A job is a process this session started, distinct from a subagent, which is why the two counters are separate segments.
The model row's placeholder while the session factory is still being awaited. The band and the splash MUST answer 'what state is this' with the same word (D1) — both resolve this one key.

The model row's word in the first-run SETUP state (no session, parked on /login). Same agreement contract as the connecting word (D1): splash and band resolve this one key so they never disagree on screen.

A standing alarm, not a reading: remote access is off until the user acts. Rendered with a danger-coloured glyph while the words stay foreground ink (tinting the words would read as 'the words are wrong'). Un-sheddable by the drop ladder for the same reason — only the fit itself can take it off the row.
